singleResourceComparison.note: Bandwidth-only and VRAM-only linear and power-law formulas are each refitted on the identical complete cohort, using the same CPU Geekbench/RAM baseline, full-VM log-price loss with equal machine-family weights, and held-out families or GPU hardware models. GPU count is applied once. This is a direct comparison of fixed single-resource models, not a reinterpretation of the earlier three-resource validation.

methodology.host: CPU-only RAM + whole-VM CPU Geekbench power law, refitted without the test host families in every validation split.
methodology.additive: P = CPUbaseline + n × [a F + b B + c V], with a,b,c ≥ 0.
methodology.multiplicative: P = CPUbaseline + n × A × (F/30)^α × (B/1000)^β × (V/40)^γ, with A > 0 and α,β,γ ≥ 0.
methodology.units: F is dense FP32 TFLOPS per GPU; B is memory bandwidth in decimal GB/s per GPU; V is source-normalized nominal VRAM GiB per GPU; n is the integer count of identical full GPUs, applied exactly once.
methodology.objective: Both GPU forms minimize the equally weighted mean across training machine families of mean squared log(full predicted VM price / actual VM price). No residual-price rows are discarded. The CPU baseline uses ordinary least squares on CPU-only log prices.
methodology.solver: Deterministic multiple starting points, projected damped Gauss–Newton, first-order optimality checked at tolerance 1e-7. No regularization or validation-tuned parameters. This numerical check does not prove a global optimum.
methodology.uncertainty: No coefficient confidence intervals are estimated. These correlated hardware specifications cannot establish causal component prices.
methodology.comparison: Both fixed formulas use exactly the same complete cohort, training/test boundaries and objective. Family and unseen-GPU-model results are reported separately; neither model is automatically selected.
